name: Aiper
legalEntityNote: Aiper is a consumer brand used across several entities. Aiper Inc. is the Cayman company in Fluidra's investment disclosure; Aiper Global Pte. Ltd. operates the global website and app services; regional sales, service and distribution documents name other Aiper entities.
headline: Aiper ownership, cordless pool robots, manufacturing and channel strategy
description: A source-backed profile of Aiper's 27% Fluidra investment, joint-control structure, smart-yard portfolio, model-specific manufacturing evidence and omnichannel route to market.
metaDescription: Aiper company profile: Fluidra's 27% stake, W&D relationship, leadership, pool robots, manufacturing partners, channels and strategy.

ownership.summary: Fluidra completed a USD 100 million investment for 27% of Aiper Inc. on 23 December 2025. Fluidra reports the interest as an equity-accounted investment, not a consolidated subsidiary. Spain's CNMC described the transaction as changing Aiper from W&D United's sole control to joint control by W&D United and Fluidra. Fluidra has a conditional path to exceed 51% if specified sales and profitability thresholds are met; that future step was not complete in the reviewed evidence.

manufacturingSupplyChain: Fluidra's April 2025 investor presentation described Aiper as operating two R&D centers and using manufacturing partners in China and Vietnam; the disclosure supports an external-partner model, not one universal Aiper-owned factory claim.

The U.S. CPSC's March 2025 Seagull Pro recall named Dongguan Yuanhong Intelligent Technology as manufacturer and Shenzhen Aiper Intelligent as distributor for model ZT6001. Its August 2023 Elite Pro recall named Compurobot Technology as manufacturer and Shenzhen Aiper Intelligent as distributor for model GS100. These model-specific records must not be generalized to every current Aiper product.

The CNMC transaction review described Aiper as active in manufacturing and commercialization and noted centers in the United States, China and Europe, while also documenting industry-wide international outsourcing. Buyers should verify the manufacturer and origin on the exact SKU and shipment documents.
marketsChannels: Aiper's current company page says the brand reaches more than 57 countries and regions and over 10,000 retail stores; these are company-reported figures.

The U.S. authorized-seller list covers Aiper's own store, Amazon, Walmart, Lowe's, Leslie's, Home Depot, Best Buy and other digital or physical retailers. Aiper states that unauthorized-reseller purchases are outside its warranty policy.

Fluidra describes Aiper as an omnichannel consumer brand. The reviewed transaction material presents broader access to consumer and professional channels as a strategic benefit; it does not establish that Fluidra is already the seller for every Aiper market or SKU.

competitivePosition.summary: World Clean Biz assessment: Aiper combines a cordless-first pool-cleaner range with skimmers, monitoring and irrigation, giving distributors a broader smart-yard story than a single robot line. Its digital and mass-retail reach can accelerate volume, while Fluidra adds pool-industry access and a possible future majority transaction. The buyer-side pressure sits in execution: joint governance must not be confused with sole ownership, model-level OEM and origin records vary, and two U.S. recalls make authorized channels, warranty handling and product traceability material procurement checks.

developments.title: Fluidra completes its initial 27% investment
developments.summary: Fluidra paid approximately USD 100 million for newly issued Aiper shares. Its financial statements record a 27% equity-accounted interest in Aiper Inc.; the CNMC decision describes W&D United and Fluidra as joint controllers after the transaction.

developments.title: Aiper conducts a U.S. Seagull Pro recall
developments.summary: The CPSC announced a recall of about 32,660 Seagull Pro ZT6001 cleaners in the United States and identified the model's named manufacturer and distributor.
